items.readable_text:
Content:
We can plot decimals on number lines, just as we do with fractions and mixed numbers.

Content:
To demonstrate how this works, let's plot the following decimal on a number line:

Content:
[MATH: 0.8]

Content:
First, since [MATH: 0.8] lies between the whole numbers [MATH: 0] and [MATH: 1,] we start by creating a number line between these two whole numbers.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/3f7dcc16ae1d791fcc7ae33d511ec192]

Content:
Now, notice that [MATH: 0.8] has one decimal place. In other words, the decimal part goes up to tenths. So, we split the line segment between [MATH: 0] and [MATH: 1] into [MATH: 10] equal parts. Each part gives [MATH: \dfrac{1}{10} = 0.1] (one-tenth) of a whole.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/611364ce4c09179699910ebbc5a5976f]

Content:
The decimal [MATH: {\color{red}0}.\!{\color{blue}8}] has [MATH: {\color{red}0}] ones and [MATH: {\color{blue}8}] tenths.
So, we start at the point [MATH: \color{red}0] and move [MATH: \color{blue}8] steps to the right:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/21bd33796170aeab30a24c5bd696e64d]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that the decimal [MATH: 0.8] plotted on a number line looks as follows:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4c8ebcb6bca27b01fdf839dfadceae49]

Content:
Let's now look at an example of a decimal containing a whole number part and a decimal part.
